key_improvement_areas.rationale: 8 warm color violations across CSS and 3D scenes break the cold Y2K dark-cyan palette — the single most visible aesthetic defect
Fog is the defining PS1 horror technique per 5 of 6 video sources; 3 of 4 scenes have fog bugs (wrong type, wrong density, wrong color)
CSS scanlines and chromatic aberration are applied ON TOP of WebGL shader effects causing double-processing artifacts — Phase A BUG-02
WebGL shader already has 6 of 7 effects but missing barrel distortion; video research confirms multi-texture CRT compositing as gold standard
3 of 6 video sources identify sparse audio as critical to PS1 horror loneliness; no audio system currently exists

noise_grain.note: Procedural rand(); texture-based would be higher quality

chromatic_aberration.note: Also present in crt.css text-shadow (DUPLICATE — BUG-02)

barrel_distortion.note: Required for full CRT emulation per Source 3 (WebGL CRT video)

snow_bridge.primary_issue: Warm streetlight + flat black Fog (needs FogExp2)

blizzard_street.primary_issue: Warm purple fog + warm emergency lights

consensus_themes: Fog is the defining PS1 horror technique — implement aggressively in all scenes
CRT requires multi-effect compositing, not single-effect overlay
Low-res textures + point filtering are structural requirements, not cosmetic
Cold color palette is non-negotiable for horror atmosphere
Loneliness via minimal sound design creates more tension than populated environments

contradictions_resolved.resolution: Not applicable to Three.js; manually construct low-poly geometry
WebGL shader is authoritative; CSS reduced to non-WebGL fallback only

key_technical_references.topic: Haunted PS1 Renderer global volume effects
